description: Curated, source-linked policy metadata and short paraphrases for a UAE university teaching and teaching-assistant prototype.
limitations: This seed corpus is a selective research aid, not full legal or policy ingestion, legal advice, or a compliance certification.
Applicability depends on the institution, emirate, jurisdiction, data, activity, current law, and institutional rules; consult the original sources and qualified advisers.
Guidance and international examples do not automatically create UAE legal obligations. School-specific sources do not automatically govern universities.
Sources and translations may change; verify current authoritative texts and implementing instruments before relying on them.

entries.title: Federal Decree by Law No. (45) of 2021 Concerning the Protection of Personal Data
entries.authority: United Arab Emirates Government, UAE Legislation
entries.scope: Federal personal-data framework, subject to its territorial scope, exclusions and applicable regulations; potentially relevant when education tools process identifiable student or staff data.
entries.source_locator: Articles 2–5 (scope and processing controls); Articles 13–19 (data-subject rights); Articles 22–23 (cross-border transfer)
entries.summary: The federal law regulates personal-data processing and sets processing controls, individual rights and conditions for transfers, subject to its scope and exceptions.
requirements: Determine whether the law and an exception apply before processing identifiable learner or staff information; identify the relevant processing basis and purpose.
Consider data minimisation, security, data-subject rights and any applicable cross-border transfer conditions when selecting and operating a tool.
limitations: The law has exclusions, including certain government and sectoral data and certain financial free-zone contexts; do not assume the same regime applies to every university.
Article references are starting points, not a complete account of duties, exceptions, implementing rules or later changes; verify the authoritative Arabic text and current instruments.

entries.title: Federal Law No. (29) of 2006 Concerning the Rights of Persons with Special Needs
entries.authority: United Arab Emirates Government, UAE Legislation
entries.scope: Federal disability-rights law; its education provisions address education across institutions and include the Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research.
entries.summary: The education provisions address equal educational opportunities for persons with disabilities and the role of education authorities in meeting their needs.
requirements: Consider access for learners with disabilities when preparing learning materials and selecting educational tools.
Consult university disability-support staff about appropriate support and the applicable institutional processes.
limitations: The English source uses historical terminology; use respectful current terminology in the product.
Review amendments, implementing measures and the authoritative current text before making legal determinations; this entry does not specify a technical accessibility standard.

entries.title: AI Ethics Self-Assessment Tool
entries.scope: Voluntary beta self-assessment for organisations developing or operating AI systems, based on the UAE AI Ethics Principles and Guidelines; not specific to education.
entries.source_locator: What is the self-assessment tool for?; What does it contain?
entries.summary: The tool encourages assessment of ethical issues throughout an AI system's lifecycle, including data use, accountability, third-party methods and bias.
requirements: Assess the intended teaching use, data-use risks, accountability, external dependencies and potential historical or technical bias.
Revisit the assessment as the system changes and identify practical mitigations.
limitations: The source calls its recommendations non-compulsory and the tool beta; a self-assessment score is not a government audit, approval or certification.
General AI ethics guidance does not replace applicable law or university-specific policies.

entries.title: Inclusive Education
entries.scope: Ministry overview of inclusive education and its 2020 policy for government and private schools following the Ministry curriculum.
entries.source_locator: Inclusive Education overview, paragraphs on 2020 policy and implementation
entries.summary: The Ministry describes removing learning barriers, tailored support and assistive technology as parts of inclusive education in the school context.
requirements: Use barrier removal and suitable accessible formats as design considerations when adapting educational materials.
limitations: The cited 2020 policy is school-specific and should not be represented as a university obligation; consult higher-education and institution-specific rules.
The overview is a summary and does not establish that an individual tool or lesson is accessible.

entries.title: Guidance for Generative AI in Education and Research
entries.scope: International policy and practice guidance for generative AI in education and research, including teachers, learners and researchers.
entries.source_locator: Sections 2–5; UNESCO overview, Towards a human-centered approach
entries.summary: UNESCO advocates a human-centred approach to GenAI that protects privacy and human agency, evaluates risks and aligns pedagogical use with educational needs.
requirements: Critically review generated educational content for errors, bias and cultural context before use.
Assess privacy, inclusion and educational value when designing or adopting a GenAI-supported teaching activity.
limitations: International guidance is not by itself UAE legislation or university policy.
The 2023 publication predates later model and policy developments; verify current local rules and institutional guidance.

entries.title: Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence
entries.scope: International recommendation to UNESCO Member States covering AI ethics across sectors, including education and research.
entries.source_locator: UNESCO overview, principles and policy action areas; Recommendation sections III and IV
entries.summary: The recommendation connects AI governance with human rights and dignity, transparency, fairness and human oversight across policy areas.
requirements: Consider human oversight, fairness and inclusion when evaluating an AI-supported teaching workflow.
limitations: A UNESCO recommendation is an international normative instrument, not a substitute for binding local law or university policy.
The general principles need interpretation for the particular deployment and its users.

entries.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Education
entries.scope: England education-sector position, principally aimed at schools and colleges; the Department notes that some considerations are relevant to other stages.
entries.source_locator: Opportunities and challenges; Using AI responsibly: Data privacy; Intellectual property; Formal assessments
entries.summary: The guidance describes possible teacher-facing uses and advises professional judgement over AI outputs, data protection and attention to intellectual property and assessment integrity.
requirements: Have an educator check generated material for accuracy and suitability before sharing or using it.
Consider the privacy and ownership of material entered into a tool and the rules governing assessment.
limitations: This is an England example, focused on schools and colleges; its legal statements do not establish UAE requirements or university assessment rules.
The guidance is updated over time; the linked page was last updated on 12 August 2025.
